(ORAL)
In W.P. Nos.18217 of 2011 and 26350 of 2018, the petitioner is the Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, Ramachandrapuram, Hyderabad (BHEL).
W.P. No.25787 of 2011 is filed by one Aliyar Khan and another against the petitioner - BHEL in W.P. Nos.18217 of 2011 and 26350 of 2018.
2. W.P. No.18217 of 2011 is a comprehensive writ petition and the decision in this writ petition will have bearing on the other two writ petitions.
Hence, the facts in W.P. No.18217 of 2011 are referred to for disposal of these three writ petitions.

3.1. The case of the BHEL is that it is a Government of India Company established at Ramachandrapuram in 1962-63 for the purpose of manufacturing Heavy Electircal Equipment such as Turbine, Generator of various capacities for generation of power.

For the purpose of establishing the petitioner company - BHEL, respondent No.1 - State of Andhra Pradesh, represented by the Collector, Medak District, Sanga Reddy, on the proposals submitted by the Ministry of Industries,
Union of India, acquired vast extents of land in various villages in Medak and Ranga Reddy Districts.

3.2. In the present writ petition, the petitioner is concerned with the land in Survey Nos.869, 870,
876, 877 to 882 of Ameenpur Village admeasuring Acs.11-22 guntas; through G.O.Rt.No.238,
Industries Department, dated 11.09.1963 and G.O. Rt. No.16, Industries Department dated 11.01.1964, acquisition of subject land was initiated.

The Inamdars of the village have filed W.P.
No.1380 of 1964 before this Court questioning the action of the respondents therein in initiating land acquisition proceedings.
By the order dated 17.02.1967, W.P. No.1380 of 1964 was dismissed by this Court.
Challenging the same, W.A. No.37 of 1967 was preferred which was also dismissed by the order dated 25.09.1969.
3.3. The petitioner - BHEL constructed a Sewage Treatment and Disposal Plant (STDP) in Survey No.870 etc., and this area was delineated through a compound wall.
The area outside the compound wall continued to be in possession of the BHEL and name of the BHEL is reflected in the revenue records.
The ROR copies for the years 1973-74, 1979-80 and 1989-90 show name of the BHEL in the possession column.

The BHEL did not notice the proceedings pending on the above file,
as a result,
behind its back, ORC was obtained by the unofficial respondents.

3.5. Based upon the ORC Proceedings, the unofficial respondents have filed O.S. No. 59 of 2010 on the file of the learned Principal District Judge, Medak District at Sanga Reddy for the relief of recovery of possession of an extent of Ac.0-32 guntas in Survey Nos.870 and 878 out of the total extent of Acs.2-13 guntas in Ameenpur Revenue Village.

sentences.text: At that point of time, the BHEL came to know that in respect of the land that vested in it has been adversely affected and attempts were being made to recover possession from the BHEL and claim adverse right against it.

Upon verification of its records and actual ground position, the BHEL was compelled to prefer appeal before respondent No.2 - the Joint Collector, Medak, Sanga Reddy to protect its interest against the activities of the unofficial respondents.
The appeal has been taken on file as Case No.F3/344/2011-F3/5/Inam/2011.
On 13.01.2011, respondent No.2 granted stay of the ORC granted on 27.06.2007 r/w 30.06.2007.

The appeal has been taken on file without reference to the alleged delay in filing the appeal inasmuch as the BHEL was not a party before respondent No.3, however,
an application for condonation of delay has been filed to avoid technical defect in the matter.
The unofficial respondents have filed a counter affidavit before respondent No.2.
In the course of enquiry, with the permission of respondent No.2, the record was permitted to be perused by the officers of the BHEL.
The appeal was posted to 07.04.2011 and at request, it was adjourned to 05.05.2011 for arguments in the main appeal.
The perusal of the record indicated that there has been deliberate suppression and misleading of facts before the primary authority by the unofficial respondents.
The proceedings before respondent No.3 had been concluded behind the back of the BHEL.
Had the BHEL was issued notice before the primary authority or in the course of enquiry

,
copies of the documents relied upon by the rival claims would have been furnished at the relevant stage.
The case of appellant could be considered if the material upon which ORC is granted is furnished to the BHEL.

The efforts to collect copies from the unofficial respondents failed and alternatively the BHEL was advised to apply for certified copies of all the relevant documents under an application for that purpose, and with great difficulty, the same was presented in the Inward Section on 26.04.2011 and 27.04.2011 before respondent Nos.3 and 2 respectively.
Respondent No.2 being the appellate authority should not have hastened to hear the appeal contrary to the law and against the principles of natural justice.

3.6. The BHEL filed W.P. No. 13466 of 2011 with the following prayer:
".... to issue a Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of a Writ of Mandamus, directing Respondent Nos. 1 to 3 to consider and furnish Certified Copies Aliyar Khan, Medak Dist And Another vs Executive Director, Bhel, Hyd And 2 ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24583053/

3.7. The Interim Prayer vide W.P.M.P No. 16329 of 2011 is as under:
"to DIRECT the Respondent Nos.2 and 3 herein to furnish the Certified Copies of Documents, proceedings requested by the Writ Petitioner through Applications dated 26.04.2011 and 27.04.2011 and afford reasonable opportunity before disposing of the appeal No. F3/344/2011-F3/5/Inam/2011, pending on the file of 2nd Respondent and pass such other or further orders as this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the circumstances of the case."
3.8.

On 29.04.2011, this Court has granted interim order vide W.P.M.P. No.16329 of 2011 which is as under:
"INTERIM DIRECTION AS PRAYED FOR."

3.9. On 05.05.2011, the learned counsel for the BHEL submitting a copy of the interim order in W.P.M.P.No.16329 of 2011 dated 29.04.2011, requested for issuance of certified copies as directed by this Court.

Surprisingly, respondent No.2 by the order dated 05.05.2011 returned the appeal itself observing as under:
"This Court has proceeded earlier on the premise that there has been no delay because it was alleged that the appeal petition was filed immediately after knowledge.
However on close look, the actual date of knowledge and the incident causing knowledge were missing.
As such the BHEL authorities are advised to rectify the defects in their appeal petition and condonation of delay petition and re- submit the same as expeditiously as possible.

Regarding the interim direction given by the Hon'ble High Court of A.P., Hyderabad in W.P.M.P. No. 16329 of 2011 in W.P. NO. 13466 of 2011, the BHEL Authorities have applied for totally (56) documents.
Some of the record pertains to RDOs office, Sanga Reddy, some of the record pertains to Collectorate and some record pertains to Special Deputy Collector (LA) Industries, Hyderabad.

As such the BHEL Authorities are directed to apply for the certified copies of duly segregating the documents required office wise to enable to provide the same."
3.10.
On 12.05.2011, the BHEL resubmitted the appeal and the matter stood posted to 23.06.2011.

However, respondent No.2 without considering and by relying upon the documents and extraneous matters, by adopting a strange procedure, finds that the BHEL is not a proper and necessary party,

4.1. As per the counter affidavit of respondent No.4, it is the case of the respondents that the BHEL is neither owner nor possessor of the lands in question, as such, has no right whatsoever at any point of time pursuant to acquisition proceedings under the Gazette dated 25.09.1963 and 18.01.1964 till date.
The BHEL failed to plead and prove about its ownership and possession over the lands in question before respondent No.2.
The appeal preferred by the BHEL before respondent No.2 is barred by limitation.

On receipt of notice in the appeal, respondent No.4 pointed out the unjust and illegal action of the BHEL before respondent No.2 and the mistakes committed by the authorities, as such, it is the duty of respondent No.2 to correct the mistakes committed by the of order status quo ante and relegate back the parties to the date of mistake based on the settled procedure of law.
The BHEL approached respondent No.2 with unclean hands and failed to rectify the defects.

The land admeasuring Acs.6-36 guntas, for which ORC was given to respondent No.4,
though covered along with the other lands totalling Acs.78-15 guntas in the land acquisition notification issued under Sections 4(1) and 4(6) of the Land Acquisition Act, was not acquired by the Government except Acs.45-26 guntas of land out Acs.78-15 guntas as can be seen from the award of the Land Acquisition Officer - RDO - cum - Special Deputy Collector, and the Judgement and Decree of the Civil Court on reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.
4.2.

As per the proceedings dated 8/2007 of the Special Deputy Collector, Government of Andhra Pradesh, filed by the BHEL as Exhibit P-17, the BHEL has not acquired the land admeasuring Acs.23.33 guntas in Survey Nos.869, 870, 876 to 880 and 883, situated at Ameenpur.

Further, the deponent of the affidavit of this writ petition himself admits that the lands acquired by the BHEL at Ameenpur are Acs.45.65 guntas on survey as per the certificate with sketch signed by the deponent as well as the Special Deputy Collector, LAO.

4.3. Further, respondent No.5, who was given ORC over Acs.4-01 guntas of land, by respondent No.3 by the proceedings dated 27.06.2007 is also subject matter of the appeal before respondent No.2, got surveyed his land under ORC for fixation of boundaries.
The BHEL filed objection petition.
The Assistant Director, Survey and Land Records, Medak District at Sanga Reddy caused memo to the Estate Officer of the BHEL to produce documents or its interest but he was backed out.

4.4. The notification of acquisition proceedings though covers Acs.11.22 guntas of land out of Acs.78.15 guntas, yet in reality Acs.11.22 guntas was not acquired, possession taken and compensation paid to the acquired lands i.e., Acs.46-26 guntas; the Special Deputy Collector even confirmed the same and pattadars over the remaining extent of Acs.32.29 guntas out of Acs.78.15 guntas were not disturbed from their lands.
The notification under Sections 4(1) and 4(6) of the year 1963 and 1964 lapsed by virtue of Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act.
The possession of the BHEL referring ROR of 1973-74, 79-80 and 89-90 pertaining to the land admeasuring Ac 45.26 guntas of those survey numbers has not been filed along with the writ petition.
The BHEL has no title and possession, and therefore, question of issuing notice while granting ORC to the unofficial respondents by respondent No.3 does not arise.

O.S. No.59 of 2010 was instituted on the wrong premise that part of the lands under ORC granted to respondent No.4 appears to be with in the land of the BHEL covered with compound wall but later on survey, it is found that ORC lands of Aliyar Khan, Medak Dist And Another vs Executive Director, Bhel, Hyd And 2 ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24583053/

5. Heard Mr. S. Ravi, learned senior counsel, appearing for Mr. P. Rajasekhar, learned counsel for the petitioner - BHEL in W.P. Nos.18217 of 2011 and 26350 of 2018; Mr. C.V. Mohan Reddy,
learned senior counsel, appearing for Mrs. K. Pallavi, learned counsel for the petitioner in W.P.
No.25787 of 2011 and respondent No.4 in W.P. Nos.18217 of 2011 and W.P. No.26350 of 2018; Mr.
R.V. Nagabhushanam, learned counsel for respondent No.5 and Mr. Ch. Ramesh Babu, learned counsel for respondent No.6 in W.P. No.18217 of 2011; learned G.P. for Municipal Administration for respondent No.1, Mr. Y. Ramarao, learned counsel for respondent No.2, Mr. D. Jagadeshwar Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.3, Mr. Venkatrao Ravulapalli, learned counsel for respondent No.5 and Mr. B. Mahender Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.6; the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue, and perused the material on record.
6. The learned senior counsel appearing for the BHEL submitted that the impugned order was passed by respondent No.2 in a hasty and casual manner.

The learned senior counsel has also drawn attention of this Court to the last paragraph of the impugned order whereunder respondent No.2 gave liberty to the BHEL to approach the authority with documentary evidence with a further finding that the impugned order will not operate as res judicata.

The learned senior counsel submitted that the total extent of land in Survey No.876 of Ameenpur village is Acs.2-10 guntas, out of which Ac.1-30 guntas was acquired for sewage plant treatment of BHEL vide Award dated 27.03.1968 in File No.F/1427/64.
The remaining extent of Ac.0-20 guntas in Survey No.876 was acquired by the Railways under the proceedings No.B3/6346/81 dated 18.09.1986.

Insofar as other disputed Survey No.870 is concerned, the learned senior counsel submitted that total extent in Survey No.870 is 11-14 guntas and not Acs.12-14 guntas as contended by the unofficial respondents /
ORC holders and as observed by respondent No.2 in the impugned order.

It is submitted that as per Khasra Pahani, the total extent of land in Survey No.870 is Acs.11-14 guntas and after sub-division,
Survey No.870 was divided into Survey Nos.870/A, 870/B, 870/C and 870/D admeasuring Acs.3-00 guntas, Ac.1-20 guntas, Acs.3-34 guntas and Acs.3-00 guntas respectively.

It is pointed out that after such sub-division, there was no left over land in Survey No.870 and the question of granting ORC to the unofficial respondents on the premise that Ac.1-00 out of Acs.12-14 guntas in Survey No.870 was not acquired was erroneous and improper.

It is submitted that ORC was granted for non-existent land, more particularly, Survey Nos.870 and 876, and reasonable opportunity was not given to the BHEL by the appellate authority and the certified copies of documents which were filed by the BHEL were not looked into in spite of the order passed by this Court in W.P.M.P.
No.16329 of 2011 in W.P. No.13466 of 2011.

7. On the other hand, the learned senior counsel appearing for the unofficial respondents in W.P.
Nos.18217 of 2011 and 26350 of 2018 and petitioners in W.P. No.25787 of 2011 submitted that the BHEL cannot plead on behalf of the Railways.

The record clearly discloses that as against the requisition placed for acquisition of total extent of Acs.78-15 guntas for establishment of sewage treatment plant of BHEL, possession was taken in respect of Acs.45-26 guntas of land only and possession of the remaining extent of Acs.32-29 guntas of land was not taken.

The learned of the appellate authority's order, undisputedly, Acs.11-14 guntas was acquired in Survey No.870 as against Aliyar Khan, Medak Dist And Another vs Executive Director, Bhel, Hyd And 2 ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24583053/

sentences.text: Insofar as Survey No.876 is concerned, the total extent being Acs.2-10 guntas, an extent of Ac.1-30 guntas was acquired for sewage treatment plant of BHEL and Ac.0-20 guntas of land was not acquired.

The appellate authority, having verified all the revenue,
survey and land acquisition documents, held that ORC is granted only in respect of the un-acquired lands.
Out of the un-acquired land of Ac.0-20 guntas in Survey No.876, ORC was granted only for an extent of Ac.0-06 guntas.
No claim is made by the Railway Department.
Neither this is a Public Interest Litigation nor the BHEL can plead for Railways.
If at all Railways has any claim, the same would be decided in an appropriate case, if any, initiated by the Railways.
There is an inordinate and unexplained delay on the part of the BHEL in filing appeal under Section 24 of the Act.

In any case,
the BHEL is not a necessary party and on such ground, the BHEL is non-suited to prefer the appeal.

The learned senior counsel submitted that ORC was granted to the unofficial respondents in W.P Nos.18217 of 2011 and 26350 of 2018 for the land in several survey numbers including the land admeasuring Ac.1-00 in Survey No.870 and Ac.0-06 guntas in Survey No.876 of Ameenpur Village.

8. Perused the copy of the impugned order in Case No:F3/344/2011-F3/5/Inam/2011 dated 25.06.2011 passed by respondent No.2.
9.
It is no doubt true, ORC was granted for several lands including the lands in Survey Nos.870 and 876 of Ameenpur Village which were allegedly not acquired for the benefit of BHEL.

While disposing of the appeal under the impugned order, respondent No.2 made the following observations:
"In the orders dt.05.05.2011 of this Court, the appellant herein was directed to apply for certified copies of the documents segregating the list office wise as they have requested for (56) documents which are not available only with the Collectorate and are spread over among many offices.

However, the appellant herein has not produced any document while re-submitting the appeal on 12.05.2011 to prove their title,
interest and what so ever over the subject matter lands.

The perusal of Land acquisition proceedings, clarificatory Memo No:C/543/2007 dated:-8.2007 of Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, Industries, Hyderabad and ORCs issued by the RDO Sangareddy reveals that the appellant herein i.e., BHEL is neither an interested party nor an aggrieved party before RDO Sangareddy does not arise, as there is no prima facie relationship of BHEL to the impugned lands covered by the ORC and therefore the appeal falls at the admission stage itself.

Neither will this operate as "resjudicata"
for the reason that the appeal has been disposed of at the stage of admission itself."
10. It can be seen form the above observations that respondent No.2 did not decide to dispose of the matter finally.

It was unusual for respondent No.2 to pass such order by giving liberty to the BHEL Aliyar Khan, Medak Dist And Another vs Executive Director, Bhel, Hyd And 2 ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24583053/

11. In the opinion of this Court, respondent No.2 failed to perform its statutory duty in accordance with law.
Respondent No.2 cannot allow the matter to hangover without any final decision.
Respondent No.2, without recording proper reasons, held that the BHEL is not a necessary and property party.

Respondent No.2 while exercising jurisdiction under Section 24 of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Abolition of Inams Act has to test the validity of ORC challenged before it and render its final decision.

sentences.text: The question of disposing of appeal by giving liberty to the BHEL to file documents and by further observing that the order will not operate as res judicata is unwarranted.
The appeal ought to have been examined by respondent No.2 on merits and it should have been allowed or dismissed.
Instead, a via media order is passed without finally determining rights of the parties.

12. It is not in dispute that Ac.1-30 guntas was acquired for sewage treatment plant of BHEL under the Proc.No.B3/Inams/ 1702/2002 dated 30.06.2007, out of total extent of Acs.2-10 guntas in Survey No.876; and the remaining extent of Ac.0-20 guntas of land was acquired for Railways vide proceedings No.B3/6346/81 dated 18.09.1986.
Thus, prima facie, there is no left over land in Survey No.876 of Ameenpur Village.

Similarly, the claim is made by the BHEL that total extent of land in Survey No.870 is Acs.11- 14 guntas as per khasra pahani and subsequently revenue records wrongly reflected the extent as Acs.12-14 guntas for which land acquisition notice was given and the same is being taken undue advantage by the unofficial respondents and they are trying to make claim over the non-existent land.

This, discrepancy is sought to be explained by the learned senior counsel appearing for the unofficial respondents contending that khasra pahani is only meant to give presumption of ownership and the extent mentioned in the khasra pahani is not final.
Further that the total extent of Acs.12-14 guntas is consistently shown in the pahanies and there is no dispute about such extent, more particularly, in view of acquisition notification.
However, in the opinion of this Court, these issues should have been considered by respondent No.2 and it has failed to adjudicate the appeal with all seriousness.

An alternate submission was made by the learned senior counsel appearing for the unofficial respondents that this Court may direct the Survey Department to measure and demarcate the land so as to find out if there is remaining extent of Ac.1-00 of land in Survey No.870.
Such a course is normally not resorted to by this Court.
In exercise of its writ jurisdiction, this Court neither would enter into disputed questions of facts nor can conduct a roving enquiry.
13. As discussed above, the BHEL was not given reasonable opportunity to put-forth its case before respondent No.2.

So also writ being public law remedy, this Court also has to look into the interest of the State / Railways whose rights would be adversely affected, if any orders are passed by this Court in respect of Ac.0- 20 guntas of land in Survey No.876 of Ameenpur Village.
The Railway Department is not a party in this writ petition.
The award, whereunder Ac.0-20 guntas in Survey No.876 is acquired by the Railway Department, is part of the record.

Having noticed such award,
this Court cannot ignore interest of the Railways and allow litigation to multiply and create confusion as the same would be unjust and in violation of principles of natural justice.

Even in respect of Survey No.870, respondent No.2 ought to have verified whether the actual extent is Aliyar Khan, Medak Dist And Another vs Executive Director, Bhel, Hyd And 2 ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24583053/
7 Acs.11-14 guntas only and if there was left over land of Ac.1-00 for which ORC was granted under the impugned proceedings.

sentences.text:
It may be noted that insofar as the land in Survey No.876 is concerned,
out of Acs.2-20 guntas, an extent of Ac.1-30 guntas was acquired for BHEL and Ac.0-20 guntas was acquired for Railways, however, ORC under the impugned proceedings were issued to the unofficial respondents in W.P. Nos.18217 of 2011 and 26350 of 2018 to the extent of Ac.0-06 guntas only.
14. In the above circumstances, in the opinion of this Court, it is just and necessary that the matter is remanded to respondent No.2 - the appellate authority for de novo enquiry in the appeal.

15. Therefore, W.P. No.18217 of 2011 is allowed setting aside the impugned proceedings in File No.B3/Inam/1702/2002 dated 27.06.2007 passed by respondent No.3 to the extent of Ac.0-06 guntas in Survey No.876 and Ac.1-00 in Survey No.870 of Ameenpur Village.
The BHEL is given liberty to file additional documents, affidavits / claims in the appeal before respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 shall also issue notice to the Railway Department, if necessary, to ensure that interest of the Railways is not affected in respect of the land admeasuring Ac.0-20 guntas in Survey No.876.
Respondent No.2 may also take necessary steps to get the land officially surveyed to know the actual extent of the land available and the land acquired in Survey No.870 and 876 of Ameenpur Village.
The appeal shall be disposed of by respondent No.2 within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No order as to costs.

16. In view of the result in W.P. No.18217 of 2011, W.P. No.26350 of 2018 is disposed of directing that the layout No.200116/LO/PLG/HMDA/2015 dated 05.01.2018, which is under challenge, shall be kept in abeyance subject to outcome of the appeal.

However, the unofficial respondents are given liberty to seek modification of the layout by excluding the disputed extent of Ac.0-06 guntas in Survey No.876 and Ac.1-00 in Survey No.870 of Ameenpur Village during pendency of the appeal before respondent No.2 and subsequently seek inclusion of those lands subject to outcome of appeal.
No order as to costs.
17. In view of the above, no orders are required to be passed in W.P. No.25787 of 2011 and therefore the same is closed.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in these writ petitions stands closed.

though covered along with the other lands totalling Acs.78-15 guntas in the land acquisition notification issued under Sections 4(1) and 4(6) of the Land Acquisition Act, was not acquired by the Government except Acs.45-26 guntas of land out Acs.78-15 guntas as can be seen from the award of the Land Acquisition Officer - RDO - cum - Special Deputy Collector, and the Judgement and Decree of the Civil Court on reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The possession of the BHEL referring ROR of 1973-74, 79-80 and 89-90 pertaining to the land admeasuring Ac 45.26 guntas of those survey numbers has not been filed along with the writ petition.
The BHEL has no title and possession, and therefore, question of issuing notice while granting ORC to the unofficial respondents by respondent No.3 does not arise.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The appellate authority, having verified all the revenue,
survey and land acquisition documents, held that ORC is granted only in respect of the un-acquired lands.
If at all Railways has any claim, the same would be decided in an appropriate case, if any, initiated by the Railways.
There is an inordinate and unexplained delay on the part of the BHEL in filing appeal under Section 24 of the Act.
In any case,
the BHEL is not a necessary party and on such ground, the BHEL is non-suited to prefer the appeal.
Respondent No.2 cannot allow the matter to hangover without any final decision.
Respondent No.2, without recording proper reasons, held that the BHEL is not a necessary and property party.
Respondent No.2 while exercising jurisdiction under Section 24 of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Abolition of Inams Act has to test the validity of ORC challenged before it and render its final decision.
The question of disposing of appeal by giving liberty to the BHEL to file documents and by further observing that the order will not operate as res judicata is unwarranted.
The appeal ought to have been examined by respondent No.2 on merits and it should have been allowed or dismissed.
Instead, a via media order is passed without finally determining rights of the parties.
Further that the total extent of Acs.12-14 guntas is consistently shown in the pahanies and there is no dispute about such extent, more particularly, in view of acquisition notification.
In exercise of its writ jurisdiction, this Court neither would enter into disputed questions of facts nor can conduct a roving enquiry.
The award, whereunder Ac.0-20 guntas in Survey No.876 is acquired by the Railway Department, is part of the record.
Having noticed such award,
this Court cannot ignore interest of the Railways and allow litigation to multiply and create confusion as the same would be unjust and in violation of principles of natural justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
14. In the above circumstances, in the opinion of this Court, it is just and necessary that the matter is remanded to respondent No.2 - the appellate authority for de novo enquiry in the appeal.
15. Therefore, W.P. No.18217 of 2011 is allowed setting aside the impugned proceedings in File No.B3/Inam/1702/2002 dated 27.06.2007 passed by respondent No.3 to the extent of Ac.0-06 guntas in Survey No.876 and Ac.1-00 in Survey No.870 of Ameenpur Village.
The BHEL is given liberty to file additional documents, affidavits / claims in the appeal before respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 shall also issue notice to the Railway Department, if necessary, to ensure that interest of the Railways is not affected in respect of the land admeasuring Ac.0-20 guntas in Survey No.876.
Respondent No.2 may also take necessary steps to get the land officially surveyed to know the actual extent of the land available and the land acquired in Survey No.870 and 876 of Ameenpur Village.
The appeal shall be disposed of by respondent No.2 within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No order as to costs.
16. In view of the result in W.P. No.18217 of 2011, W.P. No.26350 of 2018 is disposed of directing that the layout No.200116/LO/PLG/HMDA/2015 dated 05.01.2018, which is under challenge, shall be kept in abeyance subject to outcome of the appeal.
However, the unofficial respondents are given liberty to seek modification of the layout by excluding the disputed extent of Ac.0-06 guntas in Survey No.876 and Ac.1-00 in Survey No.870 of Ameenpur Village during pendency of the appeal before respondent No.2 and subsequently seek inclusion of those lands subject to outcome of appeal.
No order as to costs.
17. In view of the above, no orders are required to be passed in W.P. No.25787 of 2011 and therefore the same is closed.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in these writ petitions stands closed.
